extracted.intended_audience: Early-career researchers in Oxford Physics applying for the Royal Society University Research Fellowship (internal applicants)
extracted.subtask_short: Royal Society URF internal EOI application
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and internal selection rules for Oxford Physics applicants preparing an Expression of Interest (EOI) and full application to the Royal Society University Research Fellowship (URF), including eligibility, required materials, assessment criteria, and administrative deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: PhD and post-PhD experience window
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must hold a PhD and have between 3 and 8 years of post-PhD experience at the time of the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Career breaks and part-time working are taken into account; additional allowances for some types of career breaks are available (see funder guidance, p.5 of 2025 scheme notes).

rubrics_metrics.name: No permanent academic position / equivalent fellowship
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must not already hold a permanent academic position or equivalent independent fellowship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seeking greater flexibility, the Dorothy Hodgkin Fellowship may be appropriate; applicants should check funder eligibility rules before applying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nationality and visa eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Open to applicants of all nationalities. Eligible for the Global Talent visa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No nationality restriction for this fellowship; check visa support/eligibility as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application cap per sub-department
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are capped at 3 per sub-department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Oxford Physics runs an internal selection process to choose which applicants will be nominated to meet the funder's per-sub-department cap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal EOI required materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit your EOI to fellowships@physics.ox.ac.uk, including: 1-page outline of proposed research; CV; List of publications/research outputs; Sub-department name; CC your Oxford Physics sponsor (they must confirm support).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure your sponsor has confirmed support before submitting the EOI. Use the one-page outline to summarise scientific merit, originality, feasibility and impact concisely for the internal panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor / host academic requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must identify and work with a host academic in Oxford Physics to develop their proposal. This individual will act as your sponsor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact a prospective sponsor early to confirm their support before submitting your EOI. If you have difficulty securing a sponsor, contact fellowships@physics.ox.ac.uk for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: EOI assessment criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Sub-departmental panels will assess EOIs based on the Royal Society’s criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The internal panels use the funder's detailed criteria (below) to rank EOIs and select up to the department cap for full application support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track record relative to career stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Track record of the applicant, relative to career stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels will judge publications, outputs, and achievements in the context of time since PhD and any career breaks; quality and trajectory matter more than raw quantity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research career to date and leadership potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Research career to date and potential to become a research leader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment considers evidence of independence, leadership potential, ability to build and lead a research group, and plans for future career development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific merit, originality, and feasibility of the proposed project
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific merit, originality, and feasibility of the proposed project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels evaluate how novel the ideas are, their scientific importance, and the plausibility of the proposed approach and timeline given available resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likely contribution to the field
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of the project's potential impact, how it advances knowledge or capabilities, and its significance to the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suitability of Oxford Physics as host environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitability of Oxford Physics as host environment, including infrastructure and support for career development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panels assess whether Oxford Physics can provide the facilities, technical support, students/PDRAs, mentoring and career development opportunities required for the proposal's success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements of support requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If selected to apply your application must include a statement of support from the Head of Department and two referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One referee should have worked closely with you; the other should ideally be external to both your current group and the host institution (preferably international). Invite referees and Head of Department via the portal; all statements must be uploaded directly by them. From this round the Head of Department statement will be visible to applicants. The portal will not allow institutional approval to proceed until all sections are marked complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission portals and institutional approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Approved applications are submitted via the Royal Society’s Flexi-Grant portal. Application submitted to University Research Services via Flexi-Grant (Head of Department and referee statements must be complete by this date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure institutional approvals and referee statements are completed early; the portal enforces completeness before institutional sign-off can proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key internal and funder deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal departmental EOI deadline: 30 June 2025, 12:00 BST. Application submitted to University Research Services via Flexi-Grant: 3 September. Final submission to Royal Society via Flexi-Grant: 10 September 2025, 15:00 BST.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan backwards from the funder deadline to allow time for HoD and referee statements, institutional sign-off, and any revisions requested after internal selection. Results of internal selection announced w/c 14 July; training 17 & 18 July.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding scope and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Supports outstanding early-career researchers with the potential to become leaders in their field. Funding is available for up to 8 years (maximum award £1.83M). Covers salary, generous research expenses (including students and PDRAs), and overheads.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use requested budget to justify personnel and research costs consistent with building a research group; align project ambition with available maximum award and duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support available from department for applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Selected candidates will receive internal guidance documents. Two workshops will be held to support applicants with the application process. If shortlisted for interview, mock interviews can be arranged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend one of the identical workshops; inform your sponsor and Research Facilitation team early if shortlisted so mock interviews can be organised.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equality, diversity and inclusion considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Oxford Physics supports flexible working and career breaks, and recognises a range of personal circumstances that may influence career progression. Applicants are encouraged to highlight any relevant circumstances in their EOI or discuss them confidentially with the Research Facilitation team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The department particularly encourages EOIs from individuals from underrepresented groups in Physics. If a candidate has difficulty securing a sponsor or needs specific support/accommodations during the application process, contact the facilitation team for assistance.
